title: Handshake: post-shift scratchpad
content:
Quick context (for next shift):
- Night shift; lower traffic but spiky model-batch requests around 02:00-03:00 UTC due to partner ingestion jobs.
- Primary surface: hosted-api (text-generation/chat endpoints) + a small Dedicated pool serving a pinned 13B quantized model for AcmeCorp tests.
- Current standing incidents: none open in PagerDuty, but there are a few 'soft' items below.

Recent anomalies observed (notes + mitigation):
- 23:40 UTC: intermittent 500s from endpoint /v1/generate (region us-west1). Root cause: autoscaler failing to spin up new worker due to repeated image pull timeouts.
  - Temporary mitigation: manually started replacement node via infra-tool (infra start-worker --region us-west1 --type g4dn-xlarge), which accepted traffic after ~90s.
  - Longer-term: filing Infra ticket to investigate registry timeouts (linked_artifact SRE-4821).

- 01:55 UTC: token-latency spike (p95 -> 1.8s from baseline 0.6s) on streaming responses for long-context prompts (>2k tokens).
  - Observed increased KV cache misses and more frequent model re-attach events. Suspected cause: recent canary (rollout/2024-11-29) changed cache eviction TTL.
  - Workaround: forcing lower seq_limit on canary route for now (console -> routes -> edit -> seq_limit=1024) until canary patch is reverted.

Operational checklist (quick actions for takeover):
1) Check PagerDuty (PD) queue 'prod-inference' — acknowledge any new alerts and add brief note in PD incident.
2) Console -> Routes -> Alerts: verify that broken routes have fallback enabled (ModelFallback: enabled).
3) Infra dashboard -> Node Pool us-west1: check image-pull failure count. If >5 in last hour, escalate to infra-team (tag @infra on Slack).
4) Autoscaler logs: tail /var/log/autoscaler/current.log for 10m. Command: ssh jump@ops && sudo journalctl -u autoscaler -n 200 -f.
5) KV cache health: run kv-stats tool (kv-stats --model pinned-13b --region us-west1). Look for cache hit ratio <0.6.
6) Cost note: Dedicated pool is in burst mode; if we hit >85% utilization, accept increased spend or notify on-call lead (Maya).

Commands & snippets (saveable):
- Restart failing worker: infra restart-worker --id <worker-id> --region us-west1
- Drain node for maintenance: infra drain-node --id <node-id> && infra cordon-node --id <node-id>
- Revert canary rollout: api rollouts revert --route /v1/generate --to-tag stable-2024-11-15
- Temporary scale-up: infra scale-pool --pool dedicated-us-west1 --replicas 3

Open TODOs (must-not-forget):
- Add an alert for 'image_pull_error_rate' to hit Slack channel #infra-ops (right now only emailed). Priority: medium.
- Confirm with release-engineering whether the canary change to KV TTL was intentional (ping @jamal).
- Draft a short post-mortem template for the 23:40 image pull flaps if the issue repeats.

Notes for next shift (questions / handover):
- Did you see any retriggers from the partner ingestion at 02:00? If yes, copy timestamp and sample payload to S3://ops-dumps/partners/nov30/ for debug.
- If autoscaler fails to start a node 2x in a row, escalate to on-call infra (pager: infra-esc).

Known quirks & little tricks (learned):
- When model re-attach happens frequently, restarting a single worker sometimes reduces p95 immediately (we think kernel-level mem fragmentation plus cuda context spin-up). Try infra restart-worker for the worker with highest vmem.
- For quick token-level debugging use the token-inspect tool (token-inspect --request-id <id>) — it shows prefix cache hits per-layer which is helpful when debugging long-context regressions.

Escalation matrix (quick):
- infra-image-pull / registry timeouts -> infra on-call -> if no ack in 10m escalate to infra-lead.
- model-quality regression (lossy outputs, obvious hallucination spikes) -> applied-ml -> if production impact >5% queries, page product-ml@redwood.

Random scribbles / brain-dump (unstructured):
- Think about adding a per-route 'burst_capacity' knob in Console that doesn't change billing until actually used (UI flag + behind-the-scenes budget cap). Good convo item for product-hosted-api.
- Could we add a 'sticky-kv' mode that pins some prefixes in-memory for high-value partners? Might reduce re-attaches.

Wrap-up (handoff lines to include in Slack at shift change):
- TL;DR: no active PD incidents. Watch image pull errors in us-west1; token-latency spike mitigated by reverting canary TTL. Default route stable.
- Actions for you: monitor infra image-pull count, keep an eye on kv hit ratio, and if partner ingestion retriggers, capture payload to S3 and notify Maya.

Questions for you (next on-call):
- If you need to scale Dedicated pool for testing, please coordinate with Billing (billing@redwood) — we have a soft cap.
- Flag anything that looks like persistent registry failures (timestamp + worker-id).

Signed off: Priya (night shift)
